author: Claude (English teacher role)
basis: Replaces the workbook B2 column, which read as written academic prose rather than a spoken talk (openers such as 'Fundamentally,' 'Furthermore,' 'Ultimately,') and failed every slide of the v2 gate. Facts unchanged. Level is carried by syntax — cleft on slides 5 and 18, fronted inversion on slide 12, participle clauses and a reduced relative — rather than by academic vocabulary, which was the defect an external examiner found in the first reference mission.

slides.1: On paper our rankings are among the most impressive in the world. What I want to examine this morning is whether that reputation survives contact with an ordinary classroom in a provincial township.
slides.2: Goal four commits every country to learning that continues for life and excludes nobody, whatever a household earns and wherever it sits on the map. Our entire technology sector rests on that commitment, though its ethics are seldom debated.
slides.3: Decades of public expenditure on science and mathematics produced the wealth we currently enjoy. With births now at their lowest recorded level, whether that spending still lands where it is most needed has become a legitimate question.
slides.4: The demographic arithmetic is stark: 300,000 babies in 1990 against fewer than 140,000 last year. Country schools are consequently being closed, and the children left behind face a much longer journey to an ordinary lesson.
slides.5: What the laboratory period actually trains is recall, and invention quietly disappears from the room. Pupils who might have developed a genuine passion abandon the subject early, which is poor preparation for anyone facing a warming planet.
slides.6: A child in Taipei works in a well-equipped laboratory, while a child two hours away borrows whatever the school possesses. Government surveys measure that difference at around 30%, which a system may be designed to narrow or tolerate.
slides.7: Consider the achievements. Nobody pays a cent for the first twelve compulsory years and 99% complete the primary stage, positioning us at the upper end of the OECD, though access was never identical to quality.
slides.8: Public money now reaches 96% of five-year-olds from disadvantaged households, placing them inside a preschool classroom. It is there that the counting and the questioning science subsequently depends upon are first acquired.
slides.9: Completion figures recorded here sit above the world average at every stage, and stronger preparation for teachers has raised the quality of ordinary lessons. Averages of that size, however, can disguise how sharply one county differs from another.
slides.10: A response is under way. Funding has been redirected towards inquiry-led science, which turns a period into something a class constructs rather than something it reads, and programming reaches pupils years before it reached us.
slides.11: Over 80% of institutions have adopted digital teaching, and modelling software lets a hypothesis be tried without a bench. That mirrors how our chip designers work, though using it responsibly still has to be taught.
slides.12: The strongest candidates compete for placements inside the largest manufacturers, and the people supervising them hand over work with real consequences. Only when a deadline is genuine does the distance between a lecture and a clean-energy job close.
slides.13: Everything taught in these classrooms underpins exports of roughly 500 billion US dollars each year. The identical competence will be required to construct the defences a hotter, wetter island is certain to need.
slides.14: Progress has not been uniform. Only 30% of engineering graduates are female, because a belief that machines belong to men has proved remarkably durable, and prejudice of that kind wastes ability this country cannot afford to lose.
slides.15: If these divisions are left unaddressed they will widen, and an entire cohort of ability disappears unused. Those of us already at university ought to be asking whether regulation can move as fast as automated labour.
slides.16: How well a society withstands shock is determined in its classrooms. Absent genuine structural reform, our advantage in sustainable technology will erode by degrees, because what is taught must match the century being lived.
slides.17: Pulling the evidence together, the picture holds real advance beside difficulties that refuse to shift. Science drives national development and attendance remains strong, yet fairness for every pupil is still outstanding.
slides.18: International rankings flatter us considerably. What those papers assess is memory, not imagination and certainly not fairness, so real reform means shifting the incentive rather than adding one more test to the calendar.
slides.19: Looking forward, science that includes everyone has to find the populations we routinely miss, and the syllabus demands thorough revision. No course should leave its content unconnected to the world beyond the window.
slides.20: So I am asking something specific of you. Argue about education policy in public, volunteer where a country school is short of people, or press your faculty to reconsider what it delivers.
